newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan rupee ends weaker after ranged trade.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan rupee ends weaker after ranged trade.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee closed slightly lower against the dollar on Tuesday in lethargic trade dominated by worries about volatile local interest rates, dealers said.
"The rupee moved in a very narrow range," said a European bank dealer. "There was no big demand for dollars with very few banks doing import covering.

The rupee ended at 55.77 on limited import covering but off the day's low of 55.79. It opened the day at 55.75 against Monday's close of 55.73 due to overseas gains by the U.S. unit against major European currencies, dealers said.

"Although the central bank pushed the dollar up banks are not comfortable with dollar-plus positions as money rates went up and they don't want to be exposed to the money market," the European bank dealer said.
The central bank fixed its buying and selling rates at 55.5687 and 56.6913, raising the dollar by four local cents.
The overnight call money rate settled below 17 percent after hitting 19 percent. The rate rose to over 25 percent last week when five big borrowers were in the market.
